permit.exempt_list_quote: 5-105.2. - Work exempt from permits. Exemptions from permit requirements of this code shall not be deemed to grant authorization for any work to be done in any manner in violation of the provisions of this code. As provided for herein, the following shall be exempt from the permit requirements of this code: 1. Building. (a) Permits are not required if exempted by federal or State of Florida law. (b) Floor covering (carpet, vinyl, tile, etc.), painting, wallpapering, cabinetwork, furnishings, decorations, shelving and gutters do not require a building permit regardless of the cost of the work. (c) Preliminary site investigations such as test borings, test pilings, well points, and soil sampling activities do not require a permit. (d) Placement of construction trailers on the job site once site plans have been approved (based on the trailer size). (e) The installation of a new roof covering, or the recovering, re-roofing, or repairing of an existing roof covering, either of which is five hundred (500) square feet or less. (f) The application of stucco or siding provided such application covers an area, not in excess of five hundred (500) square feet. (g) One-story detached accessory structures used as tool and storage sheds, playhouses and similar uses, provided the floor area does not exceed one hundred twenty (120) square feet. (Setback requirements must be maintained.) (h) Maintenance work and minor electrical work performed by a maintenance supervisor regularly employed by an owner, occupant, or tenant of a commercial building. [...] 5-105.2.2. Minor repairs. Ordinary minor repairs or installation of replacement parts may be made with the prior approval of the building official without a permit, provided the repairs do not include the cutting away of any wall, partition, or portion thereof, the removal or cutting of any structural beam or load-bearing support, or the removal or change of any required means of egress [...]
permit.note: The list (Tampa Code section 5-105.2, Ord. No. 2009-27) exempts 'cabinetwork, furnishings, decorations, shelving' among other finish items but does not name toilet partitions or compartments. 'Partition' appears only in the minor-repairs clause, in the sense of a wall. The city's permit-type guide lists 'Bathroom remodels' and 'Non-structural remodels' under Building Alterations (plans required) and 'Removing and replacing bathroom fixtures or piping' under Trade Permits.
permit.second_quote: BUILDING ALTERATIONS (TENANT IMPROVEMENTS/RENOVATIONS): Use this application type for remodeling an existing structure. Building plans are required. Examples of Building Alterations include: Bathroom remodels [...] Non-structural remodels

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Tampa job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material for Gulf Coast humidity and see the rules that apply.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Tampa offices, schools, hotels and port warehouses, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Florida's plumbing rules set the number of toilets and urinals by how many people use the building, and Tampa applies them unchanged. The table below shows what that means.
page.code_change_bullet: - **New rules on January 1, 2027:** Florida replaces its building rules with a new edition, and Tampa applies it from that day. A project stays under the current rules if its plans are submitted and its permit application is accepted by December 31, 2026.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Tampa's list of work that needs no permit covers floor covering, painting, cabinetwork, furnishings and shelving, and doesn't name toilet partitions. The city's permit guide puts bathroom remodels under building alterations, which need a permit and plans. Ask Tampa Construction Services whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.stalls_after: In restaurants and other gathering places, Florida can require three women's toilets for every two men's toilets and urinals once the men's room has more than two. Licensed restaurants may be exempt, so confirm with Tampa Construction Services. Outdoor seating counts toward the number of people. At least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, the building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20. Your architect or Tampa Construction Services sets the final number.
page.install_rule: Contractors register their Florida license with Tampa Construction Services, with proof of workers' compensation cover, before they pull permits; the city charges no fee for it. Florida has no state license category specifically for toilet partitions, and a contractor whose work falls in a licensed category needs that license, so confirm with Tampa Construction Services which one covers your job. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: A contractor who pulls a permit in Tampa registers a Florida license with the city first.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** Florida has no state wage law for public construction and doesn't let cities or school districts set one. On federally funded work the federal rate applies: $17.37 an hour plus $3.85 in benefits for a carpenter on building work in Hillsborough County.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 7.5% in Tampa: 6% state and 1.5% Hillsborough County. The county's 1.5% applies only to the first $5,000 of each item.
page.buyers_extra: - **Hotels, arenas and convention venues:** finishes that match the property in guest-facing restrooms, HDPE or phenolic where crowds and nightly washdown are hard on stalls.

- The change to the 9th Edition in Tampa and the December 31, 2026 cut-off for projects under the 8th Edition: [City of Tampa, New Florida Building Code 9th Edition (2026), Effective January 1, 2027](https://www.tampa.gov/sites/default/files/document/2026/building_code_announcement_2026_9th-edition_ada.pdf). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Toilet counts are the state's in Tampa: the Florida Building Commission's [report of local technical amendments to the 8th Edition (2023) Florida Building Code, Plumbing](https://www.floridabuilding.org/fbc/thecode/2026_Code_Development/June_2025-1st_Comment/Local_Amendments/PLUMBING-Detail_Report-LA.docx) lists Broward County, Pinellas County and Miami-Dade County only, and Tampa's Adopted Codes list shows no local amendment. Checked 2026-11-24.

- Work exempt from a permit in Tampa: Tampa Code of Ordinances, Section 5-105.2, as quoted on [Construction Services FAQ, question 10](https://www.tampa.gov/construction-services/how-do-i); permit types for remodels in [How to Select a Permit Application Type](https://www.tampa.gov/sites/default/files/document/2026/how-to-select-a-permit-application-type_ada.pdf). Checked 2026-11-24.
- Contractor licenses in Tampa: [Construction Services FAQ, questions 12 and 16](https://www.tampa.gov/construction-services/how-do-i). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Sales tax in Hillsborough County: Florida Department of Revenue, [TIP 26A01-21, Hillsborough County Surtax Rate Update (November 20, 2026)](https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/tips/Documents/TIP_26A01-21.pdf), [TIP 25A01-02 (collection of all three county surtaxes resumed June 1, 2025)](https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/tips/Documents/TIP_25A01-02.pdf), [Form DR-15DSS, Discretionary Sales Surtax Information for Calendar Year 2026](https://floridarevenue.com/Forms_library/current/dr15dss_26.pdf) and [Discretionary Sales Surtax](https://floridarevenue.com/taxes/taxesfees/Pages/discretionary.aspx) for the $5,000 limit. Checked 2026-11-24.

- Hillsborough County carpenter rate on federally funded building work: [federal wage determination FL20260208, modification 1, May 18, 2026](https://sam.gov/wage-determination/FL20260208/1). Checked 2026-11-24.
page.official_names: - The rules by their official names: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design; Florida Building Code, 8th Edition (2023): Building, Plumbing and Accessibility volumes, in force since December 31, 2023 and enforced in Tampa without local technical amendments; replaced by the 9th Edition (2026), which Tampa applies from January 1, 2027; Tampa Code of Ordinances, Chapter 5 (Building Code), Section 5-105.2 for work exempt from permits; NFPA 286 for HDPE under the International Building Code, the model for Florida's code.
